description: Eight authenticated observational images: stars and galaxies, North American and European landscapes, atmospheric structure and a cyclone. Includes one ESO CC BY 4.0 Hubble photo with exact credit.

images.title: Star trails from the space station
images.summary: A composite of more than 200 exposures taken by NASA astronaut Christina Koch aboard the ISS traces apparent stellar movement during a six-minute orbital passage.
images.alt: Curving white star trails above Earth and colorful streaks of city lights near a silhouette of spacecraft hardware.
images.caption: These curved paths result from the relative motion of the International Space Station and stars during stacked long exposures, not from stars moving rapidly.
images.credit: NASA / Expedition 60 astronaut Christina Koch / ISS Crew Earth Observations Facility
images.rights: NASA/USGS observational imagery, generally reusable as US government mission media subject to NASA media-use guidance and any partner credits; final rights audit pending.
images.processing: Time-lapse composite of over 200 astronaut photographs; NASA crop and contrast adjustments retained. Source observational image resized to max 1800px and encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development edition, with input URL recorded.

images.title: A deep field of distant galaxies
images.summary: Hubble exposures gathered between 2002 and 2012 reveal thousands of galaxies in one tiny observed patch of sky. The mosaic reaches across immense spans of cosmic history.
images.alt: Black field densely populated with small differently colored and differently shaped galaxies, some spirals and some faint red smudges.
images.caption: The Hubble Ultra Deep Field is a very small patch of the observable sky; it does not depict the entire observable universe.
images.credit: NASA / ESA / H. Teplitz / M. Rafelski / A. Koekemoer / R. Windhorst / Z. Levay
images.rights: NASA/ESA collaboration; preserve the full multi-author NASA credits and verify reuse conditions for ESA partner imagery.
images.processing: Multiple Hubble exposures composited and rendered into representative colors; source WebP converted to JPEG. Source observational image resized to max 1800px and encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development edition, with input URL recorded.

images.title: Milky Way across the infrared sky
images.summary: The Two Micron All-Sky Survey maps half a billion stellar sources in three infrared wavelengths. Our Solar System lies within this galaxy, viewed from Earth's location.
images.alt: Oval panoramic map of the star-dense Milky Way in a dark infrared color composite, with the galactic center as the brightest band.
images.caption: A full-sky infrared map produced from 2MASS observations; blue, green and red represent wavelengths 1.2, 1.6 and 2.2 micrometers, not naked-eye colors.
images.credit: Two Micron All-Sky Survey / NASA-JPL / University of Massachusetts / IPAC
images.rights: NASA/USGS observational imagery, generally reusable as US government mission media subject to NASA media-use guidance and any partner credits; final rights audit pending.
images.processing: Stitched all-sky observational map with added explanatory labels; not a camera photograph of the Milky Way from outside. Source observational image resized to max 1800px and encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development edition, with input URL recorded.

images.title: The nearby double stars Alpha Centauri A and B
images.summary: A Hubble Space Telescope view resolves Alpha Centauri A and B, the nearby binary stars orbiting each other. Proxima Centauri, the third system member, is out of frame.
images.alt: Two brilliant orange-white stars against dark space, each showing long telescope diffraction spikes, with a 17-arcsecond scale bar.
images.caption: Alpha Centauri A and B as imaged by Hubble; the brilliant spikes are optical artifacts, not real jets from the stars.
images.rights: ESO image distributed under CC BY 4.0 International (https://www.eso.org/public/outreach/copyright/); preserve exact credit ESA/Hubble & NASA visibly; indicate resizing.
images.processing: ESO published image with scale annotation; max 1800px re-encoding for development edition. Source observational image resized to max 1800px and encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development edition, with input URL recorded.

images.title: Aletsch Glacier and Swiss Alps
images.summary: A Landsat 8 view shows the Great Aletsch Glacier threading through the ridges and valleys of the European Alps. The NASA study compares its extent with 1984.
images.alt: Pale white glacier winding through complex jagged green and brown Alpine mountains from above.
images.caption: Swiss Alps photographed by Landsat 8 on August 6, 2024; the long glacier reveals alpine ice and the surrounding mountainous landscape.
images.credit: NASA Earth Observatory / Michala Garrison / USGS Landsat
images.rights: NASA/USGS observational imagery, generally reusable as US government mission media subject to NASA media-use guidance and any partner credits; final rights audit pending.
images.processing: NASA Earth Observatory processed Landsat satellite image; the present frame is the 2024 observation. Source observational image resized to max 1800px and encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development edition, with input URL recorded.

images.title: Kobuk Valley dunes in Alaska
images.summary: Golden sand dunes stand out within green boreal forest in Alaska's Kobuk Valley National Park, illustrating North America's contrasting landscapes.
images.alt: Light-colored dune field beside a winding river amid vast green forest and dark green hills.
images.caption: Landsat scene of the Great Kobuk Sand Dunes in Alaska; one example among North America's varied natural environments.
images.rights: NASA/USGS observational imagery, generally reusable as US government mission media subject to NASA media-use guidance and any partner credits; final rights audit pending.
images.processing: Natural-color or processed Landsat Earth-observation image; no synthetic dunes or generated content. Source observational image resized to max 1800px and encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development edition, with input URL recorded.

images.title: Earth's thin atmospheric layers
images.summary: An ISS astronaut photograph catches the curved edge of the atmosphere in layers of warm light and blue haze beneath a crescent Moon.
images.alt: Thin red-orange atmospheric layer topped by blue and black space, with a small Moon crescent above.
images.caption: The atmospheric limb provides a natural cross-section: reddish scattering in the lower atmosphere, blues higher up, and space beyond.
images.credit: NASA / Expedition 66 crew / ISS Crew Earth Observations Facility
images.rights: NASA/USGS observational imagery, generally reusable as US government mission media subject to NASA media-use guidance and any partner credits; final rights audit pending.
images.processing: NASA ISS photograph cropped and contrast enhanced, with lens artifacts removed. Source observational image resized to max 1800px and encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development edition, with input URL recorded.

images.title: Spiral clouds of Hurricane Dorian
images.summary: NASA's Aqua MODIS sensor imaged the broad white spiral cloud bands of Hurricane Dorian as it crossed the northern Bahamas on September 1, 2019.
images.alt: Huge white cyclonic cloud system with a distinct eye over blue ocean and islands near Florida and the Bahamas.
images.caption: A planetary-scale cloud system viewed in natural color from orbit; the structured spiral reveals the dynamics of a tropical cyclone.
images.credit: NASA Earth Observatory / Aqua MODIS / NASA GSFC
images.rights: NASA/USGS observational imagery, generally reusable as US government mission media subject to NASA media-use guidance and any partner credits; final rights audit pending.
images.processing: Aqua MODIS natural-color satellite composite; source rendering retains NASA's original adjustments. Source observational image resized to max 1800px and encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development edition, with input URL recorded.
